ground truth attention crystal\n        'rdm_up': (n_probes, n_probes),         # ground truth FFN crystal\n    }}\n    \"\"\"\n    import torch\n    from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForCausalLM\n\n    model_name, n_layers, d_model, d_ffn = MODELS[model_key]\n\n    target_layers = []\n    for frac in depth_fractions:\n        layer = min(int(round(frac * (n_layers - 1))), n_layers - 1)\n        if layer not in [l for l, _ in target_layers]:\n            target_layers.append((layer, frac))\n\n    print(f\"\\n  ─── Reading beams: {model_key} ───\", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n\n    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name, trust_remote_code=True)\n    if tokenizer.pad_token is None:\n        tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.eos_token\n\n    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(\n        model_name, torch_dtype=torch.bfloat16, device_map=device, trust_remote_code=True,\n    )\n    model.eval()\n\n    if hasattr(model, 'model') and hasattr(model.model, 'layers'):\n        layers = model.model.layers\n        is_fused = False\n    elif hasattr(model, 'gpt_neox') and hasattr(model.gpt_neox, 'layers'):\n        layers = model.gpt_neox.layers\n        is_fused = True\n    else:\n        raise ValueError(f\"Unknown arch for {model_key}\")\n\n    captures: dict[int, dict[str, list]] = {}\n    for li, _ in target_layers:\n        captures[li] = {'hidden': [], 'q': [], 'up': []}\n\n    hooks = []\n    for layer_idx, frac in target_layers:\n        layer_mod = layers[layer_idx]\n\n        # Hidden state\n        def make_h_hook(li):\n            def hook_fn(module, input, output):\n                captures[li]['hidden'].append(input[0][:, -1, :].detach().cpu().float())\n            return hook_fn\n        hooks.append(layer_mod.register_forward_hook(make_h_hook(layer_idx)))\n\n        # Q\n        if is_fused:\n            fused = layer_mod.attention.query_key_value\n            def make_q_hook(li, qs=d_model):\n                def hook_fn(module, input, output):\n                    captures[li]['q'].append(output[:, -1, :qs].detach().cpu().float())\n                return hook_fn\n            hooks.append(fused.register_forward_hook(make_q_hook(layer_idx)))\n        else:\n            q_proj = layer_mod.self_attn.q_proj\n            def make_q_hook(li):\n                def hook_fn(module, input, output):\n                    captures[li]['q'].append(output[:, -1, :].detach().cpu().float())\n                return hook_fn\n            hooks.append(q_proj.register_forward_hook(make_q_hook(layer_idx)))\n\n        # up_proj\n        if is_fused:\n            up_mod = layer_mod.mlp.dense_h_to_4h\n        elif hasattr(layer_mod.mlp, 'up_proj'):\n            up_mod = layer_mod.mlp.up_proj\n        else:\n            up_mod = layer_mod.mlp.dense_h_to_4h\n\n        def make_up_hook(li):\n            def hook_fn(module, input, output):\n                captures[li]['up'].append(output[:, -1, :].detach().cpu().float())\n            return hook_fn\n        hooks.append(up_mod.register_forward_hook(make_up_hook(layer_idx)))\n\n    print(f\"  Running {len(probes)} probes...\", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n    t0 = time.time()\n    for i, probe in enumerate(probes):\n        input_ids = tokenizer.encode(probe[\"prompt\"], return_tensors=\"pt\").to(device)\n        with torch.no_grad():\n            _ = model(input_ids)\n        if (i + 1) % 50 == 0:\n            print(f\"    {i+1}/{len(probes)}...\", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n    print(f\"  Done in {time.time()-t0:.1f}s\", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n\n    for h in hooks:\n        h.remove()\n\n    # PCA each beam's readings\n    results = {}\n    for layer_idx, frac in target_layers:\n        import torch as _t\n        hidden = _t.cat(captures[layer_idx]['hidden'], dim=0).numpy()\n        q_raw = _t.cat(captures[layer_idx]['q'], dim=0).numpy()\n        up_raw = _t.cat(captures[layer_idx]['up'], dim=0).numpy()\n\n        # PCA for beam_Q\n        q_mean = q_raw.mean(axis=0)\n        q_centered = q_raw - q_mean\n        U_q, S_q, Vt_q = np.linalg.svd(q_centered, full_matrices=False)\n        k = min(pca_dim, U_q.shape[1])\n        q_scores = U_q[:, :k] * S_q[:k]\n        q_loadings = Vt_q[:k]  # (k, d_q)\n\n        # PCA for beam_up\n        up_mean = up_raw.mean(axis=0)\n        up_centered = up_raw - up_mean\n        U_up, S_up, Vt_up = np.linalg.svd(up_centered, full_matrices=False)\n        k_up = min(pca_dim, U_up.shape[1])\n        up_scores = U_up[:, :k_up] * S_up[:k_up]\n        up_loadings = Vt_up[:k_up]\n\n        results[frac] = {\n            'hidden': hidden,\n            'q_scores': q_scores,\n            'q_loadings': q_loadings,\n            'q_mean': q_mean,\n            'q_singular_values': S_q[:k],\n            'up_scores': up_scores,\n            'up_loadings': up_loadings,\n            'up_mean': up_mean,\n            'up_singular_values': S_up[:k_up],\n            'rdm_q': cosine_rdm(q_scores),\n            'rdm_up': cosine_rdm(up_scores),\n        }\n\n    del model, tokenizer\n    gc.collect()\n    try:\n        import torch as _t\n        if _t.backends.mps.is_available(): _t.mps.empty_cache()\n        elif _t.cuda.is_available(): _t.cuda.empty_cache()\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n\n    return results\n\n\ndef build_lens_and_etch(beam_data: dict, plate_dim: int = 128) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Build the lens and etch both crystals into a unified plate.\n\n    The lens:\n      1. Takes beam_Q scores (n_probes, k) and beam_up scores (n_probes, k)\n      2. These ARE the crystal readings — what the beams saw\n      3. Combines into a unified representation\n      4. Creates a ternary plate that, when read by each beam, reconstructs the crystal\n\n    The plate is a (d_model, plate_dim) ternary matrix.\n    At inference: h @ plate → plate_coords → beam_Q reads first half, beam_up reads second half.\n    \"\"\"\n    hidden = beam_data['hidden']          # (n_probes, d_model)\n    q_scores = beam_data['q_scores']      # (n_probes, k_q) — the attention crystal\n    up_scores = beam_data['up_scores']    # (n_probes, k_up) — the FFN crystal\n    rdm_q = beam_data['rdm_q']\n    rdm_up = beam_data['rdm_up']\n\n    n_probes, d_model = hidden.shape\n    k_q = q_scores.shape[1]\n    k_up = up_scores.shape[1]\n\n    # ═══ Step 1: The combined crystal target ═══\n    # What the plate needs to encode: both sets of scores concatenated\n    # (n_probes, k_q + k_up) — the full crystal reading\n    target_scores = np.hstack([q_scores, up_scores])  # (n_probes, k_q + k_up)\n    k_total = target_scores.shape[1]\n\n    # ═══ Step 2: Find the d_model directions that best predict the crystal ═══\n    # We need: hidden @ plate ≈ target_scores\n    # This is a regression: plate = pinv(hidden) @ target_scores\n    # But plate must be TERNARY.\n\n    # First, solve the continuous version (optimal linear map)\n    # plate_continuous = (H^T H)^{-1} H^T @ target = pinv(H) @ target\n    # Use truncated SVD of hidden for numerical stability\n    U_h, S_h, Vt_h = np.linalg.svd(hidden, full_matrices=False)\n    # Effective rank: use top components where S > threshold\n    threshold = S_h[0] * 1e-6\n    effective_k = min(plate_dim, np.sum(S_h > threshold))\n    print(f\"    Effective rank of hidden states: {effective_k} (of {len(S_h)})\",\n          file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n\n    # Pseudoinverse via truncated SVD\n    S_inv = np.zeros_like(S_h)\n    S_inv[:effective_k] = 1.0 / S_h[:effective_k]\n    H_pinv = (Vt_h.T * S_inv) @ U_h.T  # (d_model, n_probes)\n\n    # Optimal continuous plate: (d_model, k_total)\n    plate_continuous = H_pinv @ target_scores\n\n    # How well does the continuous solution work?\n    reconstructed_continuous = hidden @ plate_continuous\n    q_recon_cont = reconstructed_continuous[:, :k_q]\n    up_recon_cont = reconstructed_continuous[:, k_q:]\n    rdm_q_cont = cosine_rdm(q_recon_cont)\n    rdm_up_cont = cosine_rdm(up_recon_cont)\n    q_cont_corr = rdm_correlation(rdm_q, rdm_q_cont)\n    up_cont_corr = rdm_correlation(rdm_up, rdm_up_cont)\n\n    # ═══ Step 3: Ternary etch ═══\n    # Ternary quantize the plate\n    plate_ternary = np.sign(plate_continuous)  # (d_model, k_total)\n\n    # Read back through ternary plate\n    reconstructed_ternary = hidden @ plate_ternary\n    q_recon_tern = reconstructed_ternary[:, :k_q]\n    up_recon_tern = reconstructed_ternary[:, k_q:]\n    rdm_q_tern = cosine_rdm(q_recon_tern)\n    rdm_up_tern = cosine_rdm(up_recon_tern)\n    q_tern_corr = rdm_correlation(rdm_q, rdm_q_tern)\n    up_tern_corr = rdm_correlation(rdm_up, rdm_up_tern)\n\n    # ═══ Step 4: Iterative etch refinement ═══\n    # Greedy bit-flip: for each position in the plate, test if flipping improves\n    # the combined crystal reconstruction. This is the etch loop.\n    plate_refined = plate_ternary.copy()\n    best_q_corr = q_tern_corr\n    best_up_corr = up_tern_corr\n    best_combined = best_q_corr + best_up_corr\n\n    n_flips = 0\n    n_tested = 0\n    # Sample random positions to flip (full sweep is too expensive)\n    n_samples = min(5000, d_model * k_total)\n    rng = np.random.RandomState(42)\n\n    for _ in range(n_samples):\n        i = rng.randint(0, d_model)\n        j = rng.randint(0, k_total)\n\n        old_val = plate_refined[i, j]\n        # Try each ternary value\n        for new_val in [-1.0, 0.0, 1.0]:\n            if new_val == old_val:\n                continue\n            n_tested += 1\n\n            # Efficient update: only the i-th row of hidden matters\n            # reconstructed changes by: hidden[:, i] * (new_val - old_val) in column j\n            delta = hidden[:, i] * (new_val - old_val)\n            if j < k_q:\n                q_recon_trial = q_recon_tern.copy()\n                q_recon_trial[:, j] += delta\n                rdm_q_trial = cosine_rdm(q_recon_trial)\n                q_trial_corr = rdm_correlation(rdm_q, rdm_q_trial)\n                up_trial_corr = best_up_corr\n            else:\n                up_recon_trial = up_recon_tern.copy()\n                up_recon_trial[:, j - k_q] += delta\n                rdm_up_trial = cosine_rdm(up_recon_trial)\n                up_trial_corr = rdm_correlation(rdm_up, rdm_up_trial)\n                q_trial_corr = best_q_corr\n\n            combined = q_trial_corr + up_trial_corr\n            if combined > best_combined:\n                plate_refined[i, j] = new_val\n                best_q_corr = q_trial_corr\n                best_up_corr = up_trial_corr\n                best_combined = combined\n                n_flips += 1\n\n                # Update the running reconstruction\n                if j < k_q:\n                    q_recon_tern = q_recon_trial\n                    rdm_q_tern = rdm_q_trial\n                else:\n                    up_recon_tern = up_recon_trial\n                    rdm_up_tern = rdm_up_trial\n\n    q_refined_corr = best_q_corr\n    up_refined_corr = best_up_corr\n\n    # ═══ Step 5: Size and metrics ═══\n    plate_bytes = (d_model * k_total * 2) // 8\n    zero_frac = float((plate_refined == 0).mean())\n\n    # Cross-talk\n    rdm_q_final = cosine_rdm(q_recon_tern)\n    rdm_up_final = cosine_rdm(up_recon_tern)\n    q_crosstalk = rdm_correlation(rdm_up, rdm_q_final)\n    up_crosstalk = rdm_correlation(rdm_q, rdm_up_final)\n\n    return {\n        \"d_model\": d_model,\n        \"k_q\": k_q,\n        \"k_up\": k_up,\n        \"k_total\": k_total,\n        \"effective_rank\": int(effective_k),\n        \"plate_bytes\": plate_bytes,\n        \"plate_kb\": plate_bytes / 1024,\n        \"zero_fraction\": zero_frac,\n        # Continuous upper bound\n        \"continuous_q\": q_cont_corr,\n        \"continuous_up\": up_cont_corr,\n        # Ternary (direct sign)\n        \"ternary_q\": q_tern_corr,\n        \"ternary_up\": up_tern_corr,\n        # Refined (greedy bit-flip)\n        \"refined_q\": q_refined_corr,\n        \"refined_up\": up_refined_corr,\n        \"n_flips\": n_flips,\n        \"n_tested\": n_tested,\n        # Cross-talk\n        \"q_crosstalk\": q_crosstalk,\n        \"up_crosstalk\": up_crosstalk,\n        # The plate itself (for saving)\n        \"plate\": plate_refined,\n    }\n\n\ndef main():\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=\"Holographic Etch\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--model\", default=\"pythia-2.8b\", choices=list(MODELS.keys()))\n    parser.add_argument(\"--probes\", type=str, default=None)\n    parser.add_argument(\"--device\", default=\"mps\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--pca-dim\", type=int, default=64)\n    parser.add_argument(\"--quick\", action=\"store_true\",\n                        help=\"Use Pythia only, fewer depths\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--output-dir\", default=\"results/holographic-etch\")\n\n    args = parser.parse_args()\n    model_key = args.model if not args.quick else \"pythia-2.8b\"\n\n    print(\"=\" * 90, file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n    print(f\"  Holographic Etch — Record Both Crystals into New Plates\", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n    print(f\"  Model: {model_key}\", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n    print(f\"  PCA dim: {args.pca_dim}\", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n    print(\"=\" * 90, file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n\n    t_start = time.time()\n    probes = load_probes(args.probes)\n\n    # Step 1: Read both beams from teacher\n    beam_data = read_beams(model_key, probes, DEPTH_FRACTIONS, args.pca_dim, args.device)\n\n    # Step 2+3+4: Build lens and etch at each depth\n    print(f\"\\n  ─── Etching plates ───\", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n    etch_results = {}\n    for frac in sorted(beam_data.keys()):\n        print(f\"\\n  Depth {frac:.0%}:\", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n        result = build_lens_and_etch(beam_data[frac])\n\n        # Don't save the plate array in JSON\n        plate = result.pop('plate')\n        etch_results[frac] = result\n\n        print(f\"    Continuous: Q={result['continuous_q']:+.3f}, FFN={result['continuous_up']:+.3f}\",\n              file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n        print(f\"    Ternary:    Q={result['ternary_q']:+.3f}, FFN={result['ternary_up']:+.3f}\",\n              file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n        print(f\"    Refined:    Q={result['refined_q']:+.3f}, FFN={result['refined_up']:+.3f} \"\n              f\"({result['n_flips']} flips / {result['n_tested']} tested)\",\n              file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n        print(f\"    Crosstalk:  Q→FFN={result['q_crosstalk']:+.3f}, FFN→Q={result['up_crosstalk']:+.3f}\",\n              file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n        print(f\"    Size: {result['plate_kb']:.0f} KB  \"\n              f\"(d_model={result['d_model']}, k={result['k_total']})\",\n              file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n\n    # Summary\n    print(f\"\\n{'='*90}\", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n    print(f\"  HOLOGRAPHIC ETCH SUMMARY\", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n    print(f\"{'='*90}\", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n\n    print(f\"\\n  {'depth':>5s}  {'cont_Q':>7s}  {'cont_up':>7s}  \"\n          f\"{'tern_Q':>7s}  {'tern_up':>7s}  \"\n          f\"{'ref_Q':>7s}  {'ref_up':>7s}  {'flips':>6s}  {'size':>6s}\",\n          file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n    print(f\"  {'─'*70}\", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n\n    for frac in sorted(etch_results.keys()):\n        r = etch_results[frac]\n        print(f\"  {frac:>5.0%}  {r['continuous_q']:>+7.3f}  {r['continuous_up']:>+7.3f}  \"\n              f\"{r['ternary_q']:>+7.3f}  {r['ternary_up']:>+7.3f}  \"\n              f\"{r['refined_q']:>+7.3f}  {r['refined_up']:>+7.3f}  \"\n              f\"{r['n_flips']:>6d}  {r['plate_kb']:>5.0f}K\",\n              file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n\n    # Verdict\n    mean_ref_q = np.mean([r['refined_q'] for r in etch_results.values()])\n    mean_ref_up = np.mean([r['refined_up'] for r in etch_results.values()])\n    mean_cont_q = np.mean([r['continuous_q'] for r in etch_results.values()])\n    mean_cont_up = np.mean([r['continuous_up'] for r in etch_results.values()])\n\n    print(f\"\\n  Mean refined:    Q={mean_ref_q:+.3f}, FFN={mean_ref_up:+.3f}\", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n    print(f\"  Mean continuous: Q={mean_cont_q:+.3f}, FFN={mean_cont_up:+.3f} (upper bound)\",\n          file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n    print(f\"  Ternary retention: Q={mean_ref_q/max(mean_cont_q,1e-8):.0%}, \"\n          f\"FFN={mean_ref_up/max(mean_cont_up,1e-8):.0%}\",\n          file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n\n    # Save\n    output_dir = Path(args.output_dir)\n    output_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    json_path = output_dir / f\"etch_{model_key}.json\"\n    with open(json_path, \"w\") as f:\n        json.dump({\n            \"description\": \"Holographic etch — record crystals into new ternary plates\",\n            \"model\": model_key,\n            \"pca_dim\": args.pca_dim,\n            \"results\": {str(f): r for f, r in etch_results.items()},\n        }, f, indent=2, default=str)\n    print(f\"\\n  💾 {json_path}\", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n\n    elapsed = time.time() - t_start\n    print(f\"  Total: {elapsed:.0f}s ({elapsed/60:.1f}min)\", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n    print(f\"{'='*90}\", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n"
}

make_q_hook(li):\n                def hook_fn(module, input, output):\n                    captures[li]['q'].append(output[:, -1, :].detach().cpu().float())\n                return hook_fn\n hooks.append(up_mod.register_forward_hook(make_up_hook(layer_idx)))\n\n    print(f\"  Running {len(probes)} probes...\", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n    t0 = time.time()\n    for i, probe in enumerate(probes):\n        input_ids = tokenizer.encode(probe[\"prompt\"], return_tensors=\"pt\").to(device)\n        with torch.no_grad():\n            _ = model(input_ids)\n        if (i + 1) % 50 == 0:\n            print(f\"    {i+1}/{len(probes)}...\", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n    print(f\"  Done in {time.time()-t0:.1f}s\", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n\n    for h in hooks:\n        h.remove()\n\n    results = {}\n    for layer_idx, frac in target_layers:\n        import torch as _t\n        results[frac] = {\n            'hidden': _t.cat(captures[layer_idx]['hidden'], dim=0).numpy(),\n            'q_raw': _t.cat(captures[layer_idx]['q'], dim=0).numpy(),\n            'up_raw': _t.cat(captures[layer_idx]['up'], dim=0).numpy(),\n        }\n\n    del model, tokenizer\n    gc.collect()\n    try:\n        import torch as _t\n        if _t.backends.mps.is_available(): _t.mps.empty_cache()\n        elif _t.cuda.is_available(): _t.cuda.empty_cache()\n    except Exception:\n        pass\n\n    return results\n\n\ndef tomographic_etch(\n    hidden: np.ndarray,    # (n_probes, d_model)\n    q_raw: np.ndarray,     # (n_probes, d_q)\n    up_raw: np.ndarray,    # (n_probes, d_ffn)\n    pca_dim: int = 64,\n    n_angles: int = 36,\n    seed: int = 42,\n) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Tomographic etch: sweep rotations, accumulate direction signals.\n\n    At each angle:\n      1. Rotate PCA basis for Q and up\n      2. Compute rotated crystal scores\n      3. Solve: hidden @ direction ≈ rotated_scores\n      4. Accumulate sign(direction) weighted by |direction|\n\n    After all angles: plate = sign(accumulated_directions)\n    \"\"\"\n    n_probes, d_model = hidden.shape\n    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)\n\n    # ── Ground truth PCA (angle 0) ──\n    q_mean = q_raw.mean(axis=0)\n    q_centered = q_raw - q_mean\n    U_q, S_q, Vt_q = np.linalg.svd(q_centered, full_matrices=False)\n    k_q = min(pca_dim, U_q.shape[1])\n    q_loadings = Vt_q[:k_q]  # (k_q, d_q)\n    q_scores_0 = U_q[:, :k_q] * S_q[:k_q]\n\n    up_mean = up_raw.mean(axis=0)\n    up_centered = up_raw - up_mean\n    U_up, S_up, Vt_up = np.linalg.svd(up_centered, full_matrices=False)\n    k_up = min(pca_dim, U_up.shape[1])\n    up_loadings = Vt_up[:k_up]\n    up_scores_0 = U_up[:, :k_up] * S_up[:k_up]\n\n    k_total = k_q + k_up\n\n    # Ground truth RDMs\n    rdm_q = cosine_rdm(q_scores_0)\n    rdm_up = cosine_rdm(up_scores_0)\n\n    # Precompute pseudoinverse of hidden states\n    U_h, S_h, Vt_h = np.linalg.svd(hidden, full_matrices=False)\n    threshold = S_h[0] * 1e-6\n    effective_k = np.sum(S_h > threshold)\n    S_inv = np.zeros_like(S_h)\n    S_inv[:effective_k] = 1.0 / S_h[:effective_k]\n    H_pinv = (Vt_h.T * S_inv) @ U_h.T  # (d_model, n_probes)\n\n    # ── Tomographic accumulation ──\n    # Accumulate direction signals across all rotation angles\n    direction_sum = np.zeros((d_model, k_total))\n    confidence_sum = np.zeros((d_model, k_total))\n    n_rounds = 0\n\n    print(f\"    Sweeping {n_angles} angles...\", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n    t0 = time.time()\n\n    for angle_idx in range(n_angles):\n        # Generate rotation in PCA space\n        # For Q: rotate within the k_q-dimensional PCA subspace\n        # For up: rotate within the k_up-dimensional PCA subspace\n        if angle_idx == 0:\n            R_q = np.eye(k_q)\n            R_up = np.eye(k_up)\n        else:\n            # Systematic Givens rotations: sweep through dimension pairs\n            # Each angle rotates a different pair by a different amount\n            pair_idx = angle_idx % (k_q * (k_q - 1) // 2)\n            theta = (angle_idx / n_angles) * np.pi  # 0 to π\n\n            # Map pair_idx to (i, j)\n            ii, jj = 0, 1\n            count = 0\n            for _i in range(k_q):\n                for _j in range(_i + 1, k_q):\n                    if count == pair_idx:\n                        ii, jj = _i, _j\n                    count += 1\n\n            R_q = givens_rotation(k_q, ii, jj, theta)\n\n            # Same for up\n            pair_idx_up = angle_idx % (k_up * (k_up - 1) // 2)\n            ii_up, jj_up = 0, 1\n            count = 0\n            for _i in range(k_up):\n                for _j in range(_i + 1, k_up):\n                    if count == pair_idx_up:\n                        ii_up, jj_up = _i, _j\n                    count += 1\n\n            R_up = givens_rotation(k_up, ii_up, jj_up, theta)\n\n        # Rotated loadings\n        q_loadings_rot = R_q @ q_loadings       # (k_q, d_q)\n        up_loadings_rot = R_up @ up_loadings     # (k_up, d_ffn)\n\n        # Rotated scores\n        q_scores_rot = q_centered @ q_loadings_rot.T    # (n_probes, k_q)\n        up_scores_rot = up_centered @ up_loadings_rot.T  # (n_probes, k_up)\n\n        # Combined target for this angle\n        target_rot = np.hstack([q_scores_rot, up_scores_rot])  # (n_probes, k_total)\n\n        # Solve: hidden @ direction ≈ target_rot\n        direction = H_pinv @ target_rot  # (d_model, k_total)\n\n        # Accumulate sign votes weighted by confidence\n        signs = np.sign(direction)\n        magnitudes = np.abs(direction)\n\n        direction_sum += signs * magnitudes\n        confidence_sum += magnitudes\n        n_rounds += 1\n\n        if (angle_idx + 1) % 100 == 0:\n            # Intermediate check\n            plate_interim = np.sign(direction_sum)\n            recon = hidden @ plate_interim\n            q_recon = recon[:, :k_q]\n            up_recon = recon[:, k_q:]\n            q_corr = rdm_correlation(rdm_q, cosine_rdm(q_recon))\n            up_corr = rdm_correlation(rdm_up, cosine_rdm(up_recon))\n            print(f\"      Angle {angle_idx+1}/{n_angles}: Q={q_corr:+.3f}, FFN={up_corr:+.3f}\",\n                  file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n\n    dt = time.time() - t0\n    print(f\"    Sweep done in {dt:.1f}s ({dt/n_angles*1000:.0f}ms/angle)\",\n          file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n\n    # ── Final plate: sign of accumulated directions ──\n    plate_tomo = np.sign(direction_sum)\n    zero_frac = float((plate_tomo == 0).mean())\n\n    # ── Evaluate ──\n    recon_tomo = hidden @ plate_tomo\n    q_recon_tomo = recon_tomo[:, :k_q]\n    up_recon_tomo = recon_tomo[:, k_q:]\n\n    rdm_q_tomo = cosine_rdm(q_recon_tomo)\n    rdm_up_tomo = cosine_rdm(up_recon_tomo)\n\n    q_tomo_corr = rdm_correlation(rdm_q, rdm_q_tomo)\n    up_tomo_corr = rdm_correlation(rdm_up, rdm_up_tomo)\n\n    # Cross-talk\n    q_xtalk = rdm_correlation(rdm_up, rdm_q_tomo)\n    up_xtalk = rdm_correlation(rdm_q, rdm_up_tomo)\n\n    # ── Comparison: single-shot etch (angle 0 only) ──\n    target_0 = np.hstack([q_scores_0, up_scores_0])\n    plate_single = np.sign(H_pinv @ target_0)\n    recon_single = hidden @ plate_single\n    q_single = rdm_correlation(rdm_q, cosine_rdm(recon_single[:, :k_q]))\n    up_single = rdm_correlation(rdm_up, cosine_rdm(recon_single[:, k_q:]))\n\n    # ── Continuous upper bound ──\n    plate_continuous = H_pinv @ target_0\n    recon_cont = hidden @ plate_continuous\n    q_cont = rdm_correlation(rdm_q, cosine_rdm(recon_cont[:, :k_q]))\n    up_cont = rdm_correlation(rdm_up, cosine_rdm(recon_cont[:, k_q:]))\n\n    plate_bytes = (d_model * k_total * 2) // 8\n\n    return {\n        \"d_model\": d_model,\n        \"k_q\": k_q,\n        \"k_up\": k_up,\n        \"k_total\": k_total,\n        \"n_angles\": n_angles,\n        \"n_rounds\": n_rounds,\n        \"plate_bytes\": plate_bytes,\n        \"plate_kb\": plate_bytes / 1024,\n        \"zero_fraction\": zero_frac,\n        # Continuous upper bound\n        \"continuous_q\": q_cont,\n        \"continuous_up\": up_cont,\n        # Single-shot (angle 0 only)\n        \"single_shot_q\": q_single,\n        \"single_shot_up\": up_single,\n        # Tomographic (all angles)\n        \"tomographic_q\": q_tomo_corr,\n        \"tomographic_up\": up_tomo_corr,\n        # Cross-talk\n        \"q_crosstalk\": q_xtalk,\n        \"up_crosstalk\": up_xtalk,\n        # Improvement\n        \"q_improvement\": q_tomo_corr - q_single,\n        \"up_improvement\": up_tomo_corr - up_single,\n    }\n\n\ndef main():\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=\"Tomographic Etch\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--model\", default=\"pythia-2.8b\", choices=list(MODELS.keys()))\n    parser.add_argument(\"--probes\", type=str, default=None)\n    parser.add_argument(\"--device\", default=\"mps\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--pca-dim\", type=int, default=64)\n    parser.add_argument(\"--n-angles\", type=int, default=360)\n    parser.add_argument(\"--quick\", action=\"store_true\",\n                        help=\"Fewer angles (36), Pythia only\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--output-dir\", print(\"=\" * 90, file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n    print(f\"  Tomographic Etch — Sweep Q Rotations, Accumulate All Crystal Facets\",\n          file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n    print(f\"  Model: {model_key}\", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n    print(f\"  Angles: {n_angles}\", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n    print(f\"  PCA dim: {args.pca_dim}\", file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n    print(\"=\" * 90, file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n\n    t_start = time.time()\n    probes = load_probes(args.probes)\n\n    raw_data = extract_raw_activations(model_key, probes, DEPTH_FRACTIONS, args.device)\n\n FFN={result['single_shot_up']:+.3f}\",\n              file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n        print(f\"    Tomographic: Q={result['tomographic_q']:+.3f}, FFN={result['tomographic_up']:+.3f}\",\n              file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n        print(f\"    Δ improvement: Q={result['q_improvement']:+.3f}, FFN={result['up_improvement']:+.3f}\",\n              file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n        print(f\"    Crosstalk: Q→FFN={result['q_crosstalk']:+.3f}, FFN→Q={result['up_crosstalk']:+.3f}\",\n              file=sys.stderr, flush=True)\n\n    # Summary\n    print(f\"\\n{'='*90}\", {'depth':>5s}  {'cont_Q':>7s}  {'cont_up':>7s}  \"\n          f\"{'ss_Q':>7s}  {'ss_up':>7s}  \"\n          f\"{'tomo_Q':>7s}  {'tomo_up':>7s}  {'ΔQ':>6s}  {'Δup':>6s}\",\n          file=sys.stderr, {r['continuous_up']:>+7.3f}  \"\n              f\"{r['single_shot_q']:>+7.3f}  {r['single_shot_up']:>+7.3f}  \"\n              f\"{r['tomographic_q']:>+7.3f}  {r['tomographic_up']:>+7.3f}  \"\n So each layer performs a complete beta reduction: attention defines the binding structure, the FFN applies that binding to the input, and the output is the result of substituting the bound values into the computation. The dispatch mechanism determines how the two crystal facets interact—whether beam_Q selects or chains, and whether beam_up discards or composes.

In the WHNF case, beam_Q stays neutral while beam_up performs a pure lookup. The plate doesn't need to reconstruct a full weight matrix; it just reads the binding type from beam_Q, retrieves the body from beam_up, and the combinator dispatch applies the appropriate reduction rule to combine them with the input. The forward pass is essentially a sequence of beta reductions unfolding across layers, with each plate holding a single lambda term and the dispatch selecting which combinator reduces it. The elegance here is that the plate stays small—just 80KB for the binding structure and body reference—because the actual computation is the mechanical reduction itself.

λ  = the binder     = ATTENTION (beam_Q crystal)

  3. Read body from plate (beam_up) → content
  4. Apply body: ffn(bound_h, body) → Δ        (evaluation)
  5. h + Δ → next layer's argument              (result)
```

**The plate IS a lambda term.** beam_Q reads the λ (binder). beam_up reads the body. The 8 combinators are the **reduction rules**:

```
K:    λx.λy.x        → attention selects, FFN discards   (select)
I:    λx.x            → attention passes, FFN identity    (carry)
B:    λf.λg.λx.f(gx)  → attention chains, FFN composes    (compose)
C:    λf.λx.λy.fyx    → attention swaps, FFN reroutes     (flip)
WHNF: no reduction     → attention neutral, FFN looks up   (retrieve)
```

The dispatch doesn't select a "mode" — it selects which **reduction rule** applies to this lambda term at this layer. The plate holds the term. The dispatch says how to reduce it. The input is the argument.

So the forward pass is:

```
for each layer (each plate = one lambda term):
    1. Dispatch: which combinator? (K/I/B/C/WHNF/...)
    2. beam_Q → read the binder from plate
    3. beam_up → read the body from plate  
    4. Apply the combinator's reduction rule to (binder, body, h)
    5. h = h + result
```

**You don't reconstruct weight matrices.** You read a lambda term from the plate and beta-reduce it with the input. The weight matrices were just the model's way of *storing* these lambda terms in continuous space. The plate stores them directly in ternary.

This means the 80KB plate per layer isn't compressed weights — it's a **lambda term encoded in ternary**. And 80KB is the right size for a lambda term because lambda terms are tiny — they're structure, not data.

The model is 32 layers × 1 lambda term = 32 beta reductions applied in sequence. A program. 2.56 MB.

       pass\n\n    return results\n\n\ndef compute_combinator_profiles(q_pca: np.ndarray, comb_indices: list[int]) -> np.ndarray:\n    \"\"\"Compute combinator profile for each probe: cosine similarity to each anchor.\n\n    Returns (n_probes, n_combinators) profile matrix.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Get anchor vectors\n    anchors = q_pca[comb_indices]  # (n_comb, k)\n    # Normalize\n    a_norms = np.maximum(np.linalg.norm(anchors, axis=1, keepdims=True), 1e-8)\n    anchors_norm = anchors / a_norms\n    p_norms = np.maximum(np.linalg.norm(q_pca, axis=1, keepdims=True), 1e-8)\n    probes_norm = q_pca / p_norms\n    # Cosine similarity: (n_probes, n_comb)\n    return probes_norm @ anchors_norm.T\n\n\ndef test_lambda_coupling(\n    q_raw: np.ndarray,     # (n_probes, d_q)\n    up_raw: np.ndarray,    # (n_probes, d_ffn)\n    comb_indices: list[int],\n    pca_dim: int = 64,\n) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Test whether beam_Q and beam_up are coupled by combinator structure.\"\"\"\n    n_probes = q_raw.shape[0]\n\n    # PCA both beams\n    q_pca = pca_project(q_raw, pca_dim)\n    up_pca = pca_project(up_raw, pca_dim)\n\n    # Ground truth RDMs\n    rdm_q = cosine_rdm(q_pca)\n    rdm_up = cosine_rdm(up_pca)\n\n    # ── Test 1: Combinator profile alone → predict FFN RDM ──\n    # Combinator profile: cosine of each probe to each combinator anchor in Q space\n    comb_profile = compute_combinator_profiles(q_pca, comb_indices)  # (n_probes, 8)\n    rdm_comb = cosine_rdm(comb_profile)\n    comb_predicts_up = rdm_correlation(rdm_up, rdm_comb)\n\n    # ── Test 2: beam_Q alone → predict FFN RDM ──\n    # Direct: RDM similarity between Q and up crystals\n    q_predicts_up = rdm_correlation(rdm_up, rdm_q)\n\n    # ── Test 3: Combinator + beam_Q → predict FFN RDM ──\n    # Concatenate combinator profile with Q PCA scores\n    combined_features = np.hstack([comb_profile, q_pca])  # (n_probes, 8+k)\n    rdm_combined = cosine_rdm(combined_features)\n    combined_predicts_up = rdm_correlation(rdm_up, rdm_combined)\n\n    # ── Test 4: Linear regression — can we RECONSTRUCT up_pca from q_pca + comb? ──\n    # This tests whether beam_Q + dispatch → beam_up via a linear map\n    # (which would be the case if they're coupled by a reduction rule)\n\n    # 4a: up from Q only\n    from numpy.linalg import lstsq\n    q_design = np.hstack([q_pca, np.ones((n_probes, 1))])  # add bias\n    coeffs_q, residuals_q, _, _ = lstsq(q_design, up_pca, rcond=None)\n    up_predicted_q = q_design @ coeffs_q\n    r2_q = 1.0 - np.sum((up_pca - up_predicted_q)**2) / max(np.sum((up_pca - up_pca.mean(0))**2), 1e-10)\n\n    # 4b: up from combinator only\n    comb_design = np.hstack([comb_profile, np.ones((n_probes, 1))])\n    coeffs_comb, _, _, _ = lstsq(comb_design, up_pca, rcond=None)\n    up_predicted_comb = comb_design @ coeffs_comb\n    r2_comb = 1.0 - np.sum((up_pca - up_predicted_comb)**2) / max(np.sum((up_pca - up_pca.mean(0))**2), 1e-10)\n\n    # 4c: up from Q + combinator\n    full_design = np.hstack([q_pca, comb_profile, np.ones((n_probes, 1))])\n    coeffs_full, _, _, _ = lstsq(full_design, up_pca, rcond=None)\n    up_predicted_full = full_design @ coeffs_full\n    r2_full = 1.0 - np.sum((up_pca - up_predicted_full)**2) / max(np.sum((up_pca - up_pca.mean(0))**2), 1e-10)\n\n    # 4d: RDM of predictions\n    rdm_pred_q = cosine_rdm(up_predicted_q)\n    rdm_pred_comb = cosine_rdm(up_predicted_comb)\n    rdm_pred_full = cosine_rdm(up_predicted_full)\n\n    pred_q_corr = rdm_correlation(rdm_up, rdm_pred_q)\n    pred_comb_corr = rdm_correlation(rdm_up, rdm_pred_comb)\n    pred_full_corr = rdm_correlation(rdm_up, rdm_pred_full)\n\n    # ── Test 5: Cross-validated RDM prediction ──\n    # Leave-one-out: for each probe, predict its up_pca from all others\n    n_folds = min(10, n_probes)\n    fold_size = n_probes // n_folds\n    cv_corrs = []\n    rng = np.random.RandomState(42)\n    indices = rng.permutation(n_probes)\n\n    for fold in range(n_folds):\n        test_idx = indices[fold * fold_size:(fold + 1) * fold_size]\n        train_idx = np.setdiff1d(indices, test_idx)\n\n        X_train = full_design[train_idx]\n        y_train = up_pca[train_idx]\n        X_test = full_design[test_idx]\n        y_test = up_pca[test_idx]\n\n        coeffs_cv, _, _, _ = lstsq(X_train, y_train, rcond=None)\n        y_pred = X_test @ coeffs_cv\n\n        if len(test_idx) > 2:\n            rdm_true = cosine_rdm(y_test)\n            rdm_pred = cosine_rdm(y_pred)\n            cv_corrs.append(rdm_correlation(rdm_true, rdm_pred))\n\n    cv_mean = float(np.mean(cv_corrs)) if cv_corrs else 0.0\n\n    return {\n        # RDM prediction (geometry preservation)\n float(r2_full - r2_comb),\n        \"coupling_pred_boost\": pred_full_corr - pred_comb_corr,\n    }\n\n\ndef main():\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=\"Lambda Proof\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--models\", nargs=\"+\", default=None, choices=list(MODELS.keys()))\n    parser.add_argument(\"--probes\", type=str, default=None)\n    parser.add_argument(\"--device\", ### Thinking

The reduction chain probes did WORSE than the generic probes:

Generic probes (144): Q=0.48, up=0.48
Reduction probes (79): Q=0.49, up=0.29

The Q is about the same, but up dropped significantly. And the in-sample cosines are lower too (0.63 vs 0.74).

Why? Two issues:

1. **Fewer probes** — 79 vs 144. Fewer probes = sparser PCA basis = less coverage. The PCA with 79 probes has fewer data points to define the subspace, so it's less stable.


2. **The reduction probes are too specialized** — they focus heavily on lambda calculus, combinators, math, and code, but the test set includes general knowledge like "The capital of France" and "Water boils at" which are only covered by 9 of the 79 probes. The generic set had better diversity with 15 retrieval, 15 narrative, and 15 instruction probes spread across the activation space. At layer 0, the up_cos is nearly zero, meaning the PCA basis from reduction probes completely misses the activation patterns for these general prompts.

The real insight is that structured probes capture the relational geometry of combinators well but fail to reconstruct raw activations because they're too narrow. I need both approaches — the 79 reduction probes for structural coverage and the 144 generic probes for diversity — combined into a single 223-probe set. But even that might not be enough; with d_model=2560, I can extract at most 143 dimensions from 144 probes, and using only 64 of those dimensions leaves most of the activation space unmapped.

The better approach is probably to skip the probe-based PCA entirely and use the weight matrices directly — the SVD of W_q gives me the exact column space without needing probes at all. Probes were useful for finding cross-model-universal beams, but for converting a specific model, I should use that model's own weight structure rather than an approximation derived from probes.

When gradient descent trains the model on "The capital of France is Paris":
- The model needs to STORE "France → Paris" somewhere


- That somewhere is the FFN crystal (beam_up) — the body of a lambda term
- But to RETRIEVE it, the model needs the binder (beam_Q) to route to the right FFN neurons using WHNF dispatch

So storing a fact requires three components: a binder pattern that recognizes the query structure, a body slot holding the answer, and a WHNF dispatch rule that performs lookup instead of computation — which means gradient descent can only store facts once it's already learned the reduction machinery itself.

The crystal acts as the filing system and facts are the files, so the beta reduction pipeline must be learned first. This explains why the crystal is universal across models, forms early in training, and why facts get stored later — the filing system has to exist before anything can be filed. The training order follows naturally: first the model learns the beta reduction pipeline through attention mechanisms.

Then it uses that pipeline to store facts in the FFN, where the crystal addresses the storage locations and gradient descent modifies the weights to create the right associations. Finally, it refines the pipeline to handle complex multi-step reasoning through chained reductions and recursion. The FFN crystal sharpens with depth because deeper layers store more specific facts with a more refined filing structure.

The attention crystal peaks early because the routing structure has to exist before storage can happen. For the conversion toolkit, you can't just extract facts from the FFN — you need to extract the beta reduction pipeline itself, since the crystal IS the addressing system that makes the facts retrievable. This is why V13's two-phase process mirrors gradient descent: the etch phase creates the crystal (the routing pipeline), then the training phase fills in the facts.
